description: Adaptation values every Maple Island monster species shares in the isometric 3D world: the terrain probes, the wander rhythm, the model fit, the hop landing reach, the fall landing tolerance and the see-through silhouette (radius, colour, fade, minimum cover). MonsterDef reads this table first and then the species file data/misostory/monsters/<id>.json on top of it, so a species file overrides any key here by naming it again (with its own reason). The leading underscore marks a shared adaptation table, not a canonical monster id (AdaptationChecks). Gameplay stats are never here: they are canonical (data/canonical/monsters/<id>.json). Owner: the monster system (docs/runtime/MONSTERS_AND_COMBAT_RUNTIME.md).

reasons.model_fit: The proxy (or the placeholder) is scaled so its height equals the canonical sprite height (sprite_size_px[1]) x WorldScale.actor, the same factor that sizes the touch zone and the attack boxes, so the body you see is the body you hit and that hurts you.
reasons.probe_ahead_m: MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.7.4: before stepping, probe 0.6 m ahead for ground.
reasons.ledge_tolerance_m: MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.7.4: ground must exist within +/-0.45 m of the feet at the probe (the player's step_up_m); otherwise it is a ledge (or a step too high) and the monster turns (a jumper first tries a hop).
reasons.wall_probe_height_m: MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.7.4: probe for a wall at 0.3 m above the feet.
reasons.new_heading_chance: MeowDB does not publish how monsters wander. After a stand the monster picks a new random heading with this probability, else keeps walking its old heading. Classic monsters walk one foothold line; in 3D a mix of straight runs and new headings reads as the same wandering.
reasons.turn_jitter_deg: Unpublished. At a ledge, wall or the mob-region edge the monster reverses its heading plus a random offset of up to this many degrees, so it never paces the same line forever.
reasons.provoked_chase_s: Unpublished: after being hit (and its stagger) the monster turns toward the attacker and walks after it for this long, as classic monsters follow the player who hit them, then wanders again.
reasons.hop_max_rise_apex_fraction: Jumpers only. MeowDB publishes no monster jump rule ('Can hop to a floor above or below'). A hop may land on ground at most this fraction of the hop apex above the feet: the landing needs some clearance under the top of the arc, so a terrace exactly as high as the apex is out of reach, as it is for a character's own jump.
reasons.fall_landing_tolerance_m: A falling monster (spawned in the air, or pushed over an edge the probes could not see) lands on the first ground found within this distance of its feet, above or below, in a physics tick. 5 cm absorbs the float error between the ground query and the per-tick fall step without letting a body snap up onto a ledge.
reasons.see_through_radius_m: Presentation (the camera review: 'Are cliffs hiding monsters?'). Terrain never fades, so a monster within this distance of the player (feet to feet) shows a tinted see-through silhouette wherever terrain, a cliff, a prop or a tree hides it (MonsterVisual's stencil X-ray). 12 m is a little beyond the camera's 8 m nearby-monster radius (camera.json occluder_monster_radius_m), so a monster's silhouette is already there when it walks into the fight, and it is about 4 s of walking for the player (3.0 m/s): the monsters the player can reach or be touched by soon. Beyond it a hidden monster stays hidden, so a whole lower terrace of silhouettes never clutters the screen (the 15-19.5 m field views show monsters up to ~17 m away).
reasons.see_through_hysteresis_m: Presentation: a silhouette that is on stays on until the monster is this much farther than see_through_radius_m, so a monster pacing at the edge of the radius does not flicker in and out.
reasons.see_through_color: Presentation: the see-through silhouette's colour and opacity (sRGB, alpha). A warm red-orange, the opposite of the player's blue X-ray (camera.json xray_color), at half opacity: it reads as 'a monster is here' over green foliage, brown cliffs and grey rock while the terrain stays visible through it. Subtle on purpose: it is a flat tint of the silhouette, not the monster's own colours.
reasons.see_through_fade_s: Presentation: the silhouette fades in and out over this time when the monster enters or leaves the radius (the camera's occluder_fade_s is the same 0.2 s), so it never pops. A dying monster loses it at once.
reasons.see_through_min_cover_m: Presentation: the silhouette draws only where the surface hiding the monster is at least this far nearer the camera, measured along the view. Without it every monster on a slope wore a tinted rim along its underside, where the body dips a few centimetres into the ground (measured in the real game: a continuous line under a Snail on Snail Hunting Ground I), and a tuft of grass right at its feet would tint too. At the 40 degree view a dip of d metres is about 1.6 d of cover on flat ground and more on slopes facing away; 0.25 m clears those while a cliff, a terrace edge or a boulder (half a metre to metres in front) still shows the monster.
